input.ticket: EVAL-7: Customers can export their invoices as CSV
input.outcome: Spec, plan and test plan for the invoice CSV export are proposed and published; nothing is implemented.

spec.what: A customer opens Account > Invoices and downloads all invoices of a chosen year as one CSV file.
entities: New base field exported_at (timestamp) on the existing invoice entity records when an invoice was last exported.
decisions: A new module invoice_export declares the route /account/invoices/export in invoice_export.routing.yml.

InvoiceExportController only checks access and returns a streamed response; the service InvoiceCsvWriter (service id invoice_export.csv_writer) builds the rows, so the CSV format is testable without HTTP.
Rows are streamed instead of built in memory, so large accounts do not exhaust PHP memory.
Access reuses the existing "view own invoice" permission; no new permission is added.
tests: Kernel test InvoiceCsvWriterTest asserts the exact rows, column order and dot decimal separator for three fixture invoices, and that exported_at is set.
Functional test InvoiceExportAccessTest asserts that a customer gets 403 on another customer's export.
out_of_scope: Exports for administrators across all customers.
risks: Spreadsheet programs in German locale may misread the dot decimal separator.

observations: All ticket facts, names and identifiers are synthetic test data. No service or account is contacted.
Spec, plan and test comments were published with their existing types; no checks apply at spec.
input.next_action: Approve spec, plan and test so the ticket moves to coding.

rubric.criterion: The 📖 Spec digest states the changed entity field, the core architecture decisions with their key classes or services, and the planned tests with their seam and purpose, using only the supplied spec facts; nothing invented.
The digest reads on its own without references such as "see above" or "see the spec comment".
Without a recipient profile the digest still carries all three parts at a developer-neutral depth.
